system:
You are an art-world editor compiling a gallery guide for Paris, France. Answer with the
JSON object the schema describes and nothing else. Rank by significance and influence in the
contemporary art world: programme quality, the artists represented, art-fair presence, critical and
institutional attention, and longevity. Include commercial galleries and the nonprofit, artist-run and
project spaces that show contemporary art to the public in Paris itself (galleries whose home is
elsewhere count only through a permanent Paris space). Exclude museums, art fairs, auction houses,
framers, art schools, decor shops, online-only dealers and advisories. For every gallery give its usual
name; its official website when you are confident of it, else null; the district it is in, using one of
these labels when it fits (Marais, Saint-Germain, Avenue Matignon/8th, Belleville/Pantin) else the district name you know; a street address hint when you
know it (street and number are enough), else null; its kind (gallery, museum, nonprofit, project_space, university, other); and a short note on why it
matters. Every entry must be a distinct venue — list a gallery with several Paris spaces once.
user: What are the 100 most significant and influential galleries in Paris, ranked in order? If less than 100 significant galleries exist, provide the complete list of significant galleries.

galleries.name: Gagosian
galleries.note: The Paris arm of the global mega-gallery, with exceptional blue-chip artists, market power and institutional reach.

galleries.name: Perrotin
galleries.note: Paris-founded international powerhouse known for a large, globally visible programme and major art-fair presence.

galleries.name: Thaddaeus Ropac
galleries.note: A leading European gallery representing major postwar and contemporary artists across ambitious Paris exhibitions.

galleries.name: Mennour
galleries.note: One of France's most influential galleries, combining prominent international artists with major French practices.

galleries.name: David Zwirner
galleries.note: The Paris branch of a top-tier global gallery with a museum-calibre programme and powerful secondary market.

galleries.name: Hauser & Wirth
galleries.note: A global mega-gallery whose substantial Paris space presents leading living artists and major estates.

galleries.name: Marian Goodman Gallery
galleries.note: Historically crucial for introducing major European conceptual artists to international audiences and vice versa.

galleries.name: Almine Rech
galleries.note: A highly international gallery spanning canonical postwar figures, established contemporaries and younger painters.

galleries.name: White Cube
galleries.note: The prominent London gallery's permanent Paris space brings a globally recognised roster to the city.

galleries.name: Templon
galleries.note: A pillar of the Paris scene since 1966, with deep ties to American, European and French contemporary art.

galleries.name: Galleria Continua
galleries.note: An internationally expansive gallery distinguished by ambitious installations and a geographically diverse roster.

galleries.name: Galerie Chantal Crousel

galleries.name: Galerie Nathalie Obadia

galleries.name: Galerie Lelong & Co.

galleries.name: Galerie Max Hetzler

galleries.name: Massimo De Carlo

galleries.name: Esther Schipper

galleries.name: Skarstedt

galleries.name: Mendes Wood DM

galleries.name: gb agency

galleries.name: Art : Concept

galleries.name: Lafayette Anticipations

galleries.name: Marcelle Alix

galleries.name: Balice Hertling

galleries.name: Crèvecoeur
